7	# L2f — the full-attention layer on the device, and a ladder that inverts
8	
9	**Result: the layer runs in six dispatches where llama.cpp's graph spends
10	nineteen, and 66.3 ms of its 512-token prefill graph becomes 27.6 — 2.40x, or
11	1.60x once the one row that is not like for like is repriced.** Every tensor
12	agrees: the fused projection's six column ranges to 1.7e-04 rms, the indexer's
13	pooled key to 3.1e-04, its score to 3.8e-07 *relative*, the gated context to
14	3.3e-05 against the f32 model and the layer's output to 5.9e-05 — **7.4x and
15	19.3x nearer that model than llama.cpp is**, which is the int8 activations the
16	reference brings and we do not.
17	
18	## The graph
19	
20	| | llama.cpp | ours |
21	|---|---:|---:|
22	| dispatches per layer | **19** (17 excluding the selection) | **6** |
23	| per 512-token graph, 12 layers | 228 (204) | 72 |
24	| time per graph | **66.3 ms** | **27.6 ms** |
25	| share of the whole 1164.7 ms graph | 5.7% | 2.4% |
26	
27		qkv    xn -> query, gate, key, value, indexer query, indexer key
28		pack   per-head norm + IMRoPE + the fragment tiling, for q, k and v
29		idx    the indexer's pooled key and its query: pool, norm, rope, fp16
30		score  the rectified block score, its bias, the cells and the mask
31		attn   causal GQA on the matrix cores, with the output gate in its epilogue
32		out    the output projection
33	
34	| dispatch | disp | llama.cpp | disp | ours | |
35	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
36	| qkv | 60 | 28.2 ms | 12 | **18.4 ms** | 1.53x |
37	| pack | 48 | 2.8 | 12 | **0.7** | 3.97x |
38	| idx | 48 | 0.9 | 12 | **0.1** | 12.20x |
39	| score | 24 | 0.7 | 12 | **0.8** | 0.93x |
40	| attn | 12 | 25.2 | 12 | **2.1** | 12.28x † |
41	| out | 12 | 8.6 | 12 | **5.6** | 1.52x |
42	| **layer** | **204** | **66.3 ms** | **72** | **27.6 ms** | **2.40x** |
43	
44	† **not like for like, and it is the only row that is not.** llama.cpp's
45	flash-attention kernel issues the whole [512, 2048] rectangle its cache defines
46	— ggml's own FLOP count says so — where ours walks the causal triangle of a
47	512-token prefill, an eighth of the work. On *rate* the two kernels are
48	**18.9 TFLOP/s against 12.3, 1.54x**; at our shape and its own rate the
49	reference would spend 3.1 ms there, which makes the layer 44.3 ms against our
50	27.6 and the honest whole-layer figure **1.60x**. Both numbers are real: 2.40x
51	is what a prefill of 2048 in four chunks actually costs either side, 1.60x is
52	what the kernels are worth at equal work.
53	
54	**Two more things are left out of the comparison, both in the conservative
55	direction.** The selection — `TOP_K` and its `GET_ROWS`, 24 dispatches and
56	2.4 ms — is work llama.cpp does and we do not, because at any prompt shorter
57	than `top_k` the indexer names every cell (L2e-5); counting it would make the
58	reference 68.8 ms and the ratio 2.49x. And the pooling, the gate's `SIGMOID`
59	and `MUL`, the `CONT` behind them and the `CPY`s into the KV cache are inside
60	`MUL` (479), `SIGMOID` (326), `CONT` (251) and `CPY` (85), which every other
61	block of the model also uses; none of it is attributed here and all of it is
62	**absent from our graph rather than faster in it**.
63	
64	## Where the dispatches went
65	
66	**Six matrices become one.** The query, its gate, the key, the value and both
67	of the indexer's projections all read the same normalised residual, so they are
68	one [13952, 2560] weight and one matmul — the same argument L2a made for
69	`inject` and L2d for the PLE block's value, applied to the largest instance of
70	it in the model. llama.cpp runs five separate `MUL_MAT`s over the same
71	activation, three of them `q8_0` and two `bf16`.
72	
73	**The norm, the rotary and the staging become one.** All three of q, k and v
74	are column ranges of that projection's output and all three end in the same
75	fragment tiling, so the grid is "one (token tile, plane)" and the plane index
76	says which. llama.cpp spends two `RMS_NORM_MUL`s, two `ROPE`s and the cache
77	`CPY`s.
78	
79	**The gate is fused into the attention epilogue.** `attn_q` is [2560, 12288]:
80	each head's 256 query dims are immediately followed by 256 *gate* dims, and the
81	gate is a sigmoid on the attention **output**. The epilogue already holds the
82	output tile in LDS for the softmax divide, so the gate costs one read of the
83	projection's own fp32 row and the context leaves as fp16 straight into the
84	output projection's A layout — deleting a `SIGMOID`, a `MUL`, a `CONT` and a
85	[512, 6144] round trip through DRAM. `TestAttnGPUGateIsFused` is the control:
86	the ungated output is a plausible tensor of the right shape, and the test
87	demands the two disagree.
88	
89	## Two ladders that disagree, on one cache boundary
90	
91	The plain GEMM arm runs both projections, and **they want opposite schedules**
92	— which is the finding here that was not predicted.
93	
94	Per layer, microseconds, BM 32 / 64 / 128:
95	
96	| T | fused projection (B = 71.4 MB) | output projection (B = 31.5 MB) |
97	|---:|---|---|
98	| 64 | 507 / **417** / 452 | **164** / 198 / 286 |
99	| 128 | 914 / 542 / **453** | **198** / 207 / 286 |
100	| 256 | 1476 / 1051 / **793** | **265** / 302 / 318 |
101	| 512 | 3097 / 2005 / **1517** | 508 / **466** / 519 |
102	| 1024 | 8271 / 4156 / **3031** | 1023 / 967 / **875** |
103	| 2048 | 19201 / 9710 / **6058** | 2200 / 1838 / **1651** |
104	
105	The fused projection is L2d's story unchanged: its B is **2.2x the MALL**, a
106	workgroup carrying BM rows reads all of it M/BM times, and the widest rung wins
107	everywhere above 64 tokens by up to 3.2x on identical arithmetic.
108	
109	The output projection's B is **31.5 MB, just inside the 32 MiB MALL**, and on
110	that side of the line the reuse argument buys nothing at all — what matters is
111	the occupancy a narrow row block leaves. At 64 tokens BM=128 is the **worst**
112	rung by 2.1x. Then as M grows the activation traffic takes over and the ladder
113	turns back: BM=64 wins at 512 and BM=128 at 1024 and above, by 1.32x at 2048.
114	**Same kernel, same arithmetic, inverted schedule, decided by which side of one
115	cache the weight falls on.** One schedule could not have served both, and a
116	single `GEMMKernelFor` would have cost 1.3-1.7x on one of the two at every
117	length.
118	
119	Against the whole 27-plan ladder at six lengths (`results/l2f_attn.csv`, 1134
120	rows), the three schedules together are the **exact** winner at 128, 256, 512,
121	1024 and 2048, and **1.010x** off it at 64 — where the whole spread across
122	attention rungs is 1.0% because the attention dispatch is 11 us of a 617 us
123	layer. The worst plan in the table is 1.35x off at 512 and 2.7x at 2048.
124	
125	## The attention ladder ends one rung earlier than every other in the repo
126	
127	At 512 tokens, per layer: **qt1_kt2 170 us, qt1_kt4 223, qt2_kt4 241** — 19.0,
128	14.4 and 13.4 TFLOP/s, monotonic in how much a wave holds live. The DiT's
129	ladder (§3.3) and the text encoder's both end at qt1_kt4 or wider.
130	
131	The reason is the head dim. This model's is **256 against their 128**, so HDT
132	doubles and a wave carries 16 query fragments and 16 output accumulators across
133	the whole key loop before KTIL adds a score accumulator per key tile. §3.3's
134	conclusion holds exactly as stated — arithmetic intensity is inert, the
135	register file decides — it just decides one rung sooner here.
136	
137	## The numbers
138	
139	Against L2e's CPU reference, and against llama.cpp behind it:
140	
141	| tensor | vs CPU | vs llama.cpp | |
142	|---|---:|---:|---|
143	| `attn_q` + gate, fused col 0 | 1.02e-04 | — | six column ranges of one matrix |
144	| `attn_k`, col 12288 | 9.41e-05 | — | |
145	| `attn_v`, col 12800 | 9.74e-05 | — | |

78:| [L2e](l2e-attention.md) | **The full-attention layer and the QSA indexer** — and two more things the oracle does that its graph does not say. Layer 3 matches llama.cpp tensor for tensor: the block-pooled indexer scores to **3.5e-07 relative**, the fused query/gate split to 1.2e-06 rms, `attn_output` to 2.4e-04, and the four-stage chain from the previous layer's output to **9.75e-06**. The two numerics: **the indexer's key cache is fp16** (the keys are rounded between being projected and being pooled — worth **2072x**), and **a matmul between two F32 tensors is an fp16 matmul** (3.52e-03 rms in f32, *the same in float64*, 5.11e-05 with both operands rounded — worth **69x**). The second one matters beyond this stage: **the fp16 kernels L2c and L2d run concede nothing the reference keeps.** Also pinned: interleaved M-RoPE **is NeoX on a text batch** (no sector of [11,11,10] selects the fourth position) and only 64 of 256 dims rotate, both asserted rather than assumed; the indexer's blocks are cut against the *cache* (7 tokens in a flash-attention-padded 256-cell cache make one real block of 4, 63 that pool cell 0 four times, and a spare block carrying a finite 1e9 marker); and llama.cpp's `TOP_K` is **a selection, not a sort**, which at this width is unobservable — L4's 4k context is where the selection becomes testable at all |
79:| [L2d](l2d-ple.md) | **The PLE n-gram block, and the quarter of the checkpoint that is a hash table.** `per_layer_token_embd` is **28.80 GB of 320 001 536 rows**, and a token reads **sixteen** of them — 1.41 KB — chosen by a 64-bit mix of the token and its two predecessors against sixteen near-prime vocabularies whose offsets tile the table exactly. The gather is **bit-exact, 0 ulp**, which is the only tolerance a lookup has; the block on it matches llama.cpp to **7.7e-08 rms**. It also closes L2c's one open comparison — layer 1's mixer reads a residual this block writes into — so the two stages compose. On the device it is **three dispatches against about thirty** (the key and value projections are one fused `[12800, 2560]` matrix) and **0.19% of a prefill graph**, where on the nameable lines it is 0.88x, i.e. *slower*; it runs once, so what mattered was being correct and being on the device. Two free levers on the way: the fused projection's 65.5 MB B is twice the MALL, so **BM 32 → 128 is 3.3x**, and making the channel rather than the token the fast grid axis is **2.9-4.0x** on the convolution — §5.1b's traversal penalty again. Controls: losing the conv's dilation is 1.2e5x worse, reversing its taps 8.5e5x |
80:| [L2c](l2c-hc-kernel.md) | **The fused hyper-connection kernel — four dispatches where llama.cpp has sixteen.** The lines of the reference's 512-token graph that are nameably this block go from **226.6 ms to 53.4 — 4.24x, and 14.9% of the whole 1164.7 ms prefill graph**, with the rest of the block's glue absent from our graph rather than faster in it. Two tensors stop existing: **`inject` is four more output columns** on a fused `[336, 10240]` weight (L2a's worst line, 10.3% of prefill at 31.8 GFLOP/s), and the **`[10240, T]` gate — 21 MB a mixer, the whole MALL — is consumed inside the up projection's epilogue**, sigmoid on the accumulators then the 4-branch collapse against `xn` through LDS, which needs the four streams of a feature in one workgroup and so is a **weight permutation** rather than a loop. Accuracy: all eight mixers of layers 0-3 agree with L2b's CPU reference to **1e-04 rms** (`maxRel` 4.9e-04, fp16's own step), which makes the kernel **38x nearer the f32 model than the oracle validating it**. And L2a's finding 5 reappears on our own kernel — the norm runs at **575 GB/s at T=512 and 167 at T=1024** as the fp32 residual outgrows the MALL, so "keep the residual fp16" is now measured rather than inferred, and worth ~1.5x |

is 222 ms on the CPU, 8 on the device, and 18% of an utterance.** What is open

stage in the model at 14 ms. **`PIPELINE.md`** is the z-image-turbo slice, **parked** at 14.26 s an
image with its resume points stated at the top. **`LLM.md`** is the qwen3.8-flash-next
(text-generation) vertical and is **the current work**: L0, L1, L2a-L2e are
closed. The checkpoint is downloaded (114 GB in 18 minutes,
`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/`), llama.cpp runs it, and **the number to beat
is `pp2048 391.42` / `tg128 25.15` tok/s** — decode at 65.8% of the bus, and
prefill 5x below what this repo's own microbenchmarks had been added up into.
**L2a attributed that 5x per op and it is not the architecture**: DeltaNet is
1.6% of a prefill graph and attention+QSA 1.5%, while the hyper-connection
block's glue and its `[10240, 4]` F32 `inject` projection are 43% between them
and our own kernels are 2.25-2.53x on the rest. The target is **~1150 tok/s,
not ~2000**. **L2b then built the first block of the model in Go** — the
hyper-connection mixer and combine, in `llm/`, matching llama.cpp's own
activations to **6.2e-08 rms** in four of the seven mixers of the four dumped
layers — and found that **the oracle is not exact**: llama.cpp's Vulkan
backend evaluates a Q8_0 matmul over int8 activations, which is worth **233x**
on the gate and retires L2's "fp16 tolerance" acceptance criterion. **L2c then
put that block on the device**: four dispatches where the reference has
sixteen, **226.6 ms of its 512-token graph against 53.4 — 4.24x, and 14.9% of
the whole prefill graph** — by fusing `inject` onto the down projection as four
more output columns and consuming the 21 MB gate inside the up projection's
epilogue, so neither tensor is ever written. **L2d added the PLE n-gram
block** beside it — the host-side trigram hash over the 320 M-row table is
**bit-exact** against the reference and the block matches to 7.7e-08 rms, in
three dispatches against about thirty. **L2e then built the full-attention
layer and the QSA indexer** — every dumped tensor of layer 3 matches, four
stages compose to 9.75e-06 rms, and two more oracle numerics fell out: the
indexer's key cache is fp16 (2072x) and **an F32 x F32 matmul runs on the fp16
matrix cores** (69x), which means the fp16 kernels this vertical already ships
concede nothing the reference keeps. The Go
side reads the
checkpoint: `gguf/` (1224/1224 tensors against the Python inventory), five
dequant paths bit-exact against ggml, and a tokenizer exact against
`llama-tokenize`. The plan behind it is unchanged — run the stock quant first
(llama.cpp is the oracle), then re-quantise, because **76% of the bytes read
per token are dense** and the stock Q8_0 dense allocation costs 1.7x on a
bus-bound machine. Task list L0–L9; **L2 continues with the GPU port of that layer**. All three files are rewritten each
session rather than appended to, and the current one is the file to read
first.

experiment backlog (~30 items, each with hypothesis / change / expected

---
name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect.
metadata:
  type: project
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, LLM.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),

quote the agreement.

to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].

content.text:
**L2f is done — the GPU port of the full-attention layer, which was the one open item in `LLM.md`'s L2.**

## What was built

Four new kernels plus two uses of the existing plain GEMM arm, driven by `llm/gpu_attn.go`:

```
qkv    xn -> query, gate, key, value, indexer query, indexer key   (one matmul)
pack   per-head norm + interleaved M-RoPE + fragment tiling, q/k/v (one grid)
idx    the indexer's pooled key and its query: pool, norm, rope, fp16
score  the rectified block score, its bias, the cells, the causal mask
attn   causal GQA on the matrix cores, with the output gate in its epilogue
out    the output projection
```

**Six dispatches where llama.cpp's graph spends nineteen; 66.3 ms of its 512-token prefill graph becomes 27.6 — 2.40x.** I've been explicit in the write-up that one row is *not* like for like: the reference's flash kernel issues the whole [512, 2048] rectangle its cache defines where ours walks a causal triangle. On rate the two kernels are 18.9 TFLOP/s against 12.3 (1.54x), and repricing that row makes the layer **1.60x at equal work**. Both numbers are reported.

Correctness: every tensor matches — the fused projection's six column ranges to 1.7e-04 rms, the indexer's pooled key to 3.1e-04, its score to 3.8e-07 relative, the cell mask exactly, the layer output to **5.9e-05 against the f32 model, 19.3x nearer it than llama.cpp is** (the reference's int8 activations). Two negative controls: the 63 non-existent indexer blocks must all be byte-identical copies of cell 0, and the gated context must *disagree* with `attn_pregate`.

## The finding I didn't expect

**The same GEMM kernel wants opposite BM schedules on the layer's two projections.** The fused one's B is 71.4 MB — 2.2x the MALL — so the widest row block wins everywhere above 64 tokens, by 3.2x at 2048. The output projection's B is 31.5 MB and *fits*, and there the widest rung is the **worst** by 2.1x at 64 tokens, only winning back at 1024. Same arithmetic, inverted schedule, decided by which side of one cache the weight falls on. There are now two schedules, and the pair is the exact winner of a 27-plan ladder at five of six lengths.

Also: the attention ladder ends one rung narrower (`qt1_kt2`) than every other in this repo, because headDim 256 doubles what a wave holds live.

## Files

New: `llm/gpu_attn.go`, `llm/gpu_attn_test.go`, `cmd/llm/bench_attn.go`, `shaders/llm_attn_{pack,idx,score,wmma}.comp`, `research/l2f-attention-gpu.md`, `results/l2f_attn.csv` (1134 ladder rows). `LLM.md`, `TODO.md` and `research/README.md` updated; the MODE-2 GEMM builds renamed from `llm_ple_kv_*` to `llm_gemm_plain_*` since three blocks now use them. `go build`/`vet`/`gofmt` clean, full test suite green.

Two of the three dense blocks are now on the device, taking **25.1% of llama.cpp's prefill graph down to 7.0%**. Next is L3's DeltaNet — three quarters of the layers, and the only piece with no reference implementation to check against.
